Scientific Hypothesis: In the context of the National Longitudinal Survey of Youth (NLSY79) dataset, there is a statistically significant negative relationship between time preference (as measured by savings behavior) and BMI in Hispanic men. This implies that individuals with a higher time preference (more savings behavior) tend to have lower BMI values.

4. Variable Creation: A new variable, TIME_PREFERENCE, was created to represent time preference based on savings behavior (DISSAVED and SAMESAVE).
5. Linear Regression Analysis: A linear regression analysis was performed to determine the relationship between time preference and BMI.
6. Statistical Significance Check: The coefficient, standard error, t-statistic, and p-value were calculated to assess the statistical significance of the relationship.
